summary.text: An alcohol is an organic compound that carries at least one hydroxyl (−OH) group bound to a saturated carbon atom.
The OH group strongly changes the properties of hydrocarbons, making them hydrophilic (water-attracted), and it gives a site where many reactions can occur.
Alcohols range from simple ones like methanol and ethanol to complex ones like sugar alcohols and cholesterol.

facts.label: Word origin
facts.value: Arabic al-kuḥl, a powder used as an eyeliner

facts.label: Ethanol coined
facts.value: The term ethanol was invented in 1892

facts.label: Polyols
facts.value: Compounds with more than one hydroxy group

items.prompt: A molecule has an OH group attached to a carbon in an aromatic ring. Is it counted as an alcohol?

options.label: Yes, because any OH group on a carbon atom makes an alcohol
No, it is classed separately as a phenol with distinct properties
Yes, because the ring only adds to the molecule's size and shape
No, because an OH group can never attach to a ring carbon atom

items.explain: A hydroxy group bonded to an sp² carbon on an aromatic ring makes a phenol, which has distinct properties and is not classified as an alcohol.

items.prompt: Two alcohols share the same three-carbon chain, but one has its OH at the end and the other has it in the middle. How does systematic naming tell them apart?

options.label: A number between the alkane name and -ol gives the OH position
The middle one gets the prefix hydroxy- and the end one does not
The end one drops the -ol and takes an -al ending instead
Each gets a different Greek prefix for its carbon count

items.explain: The position of the hydroxyl group is shown by a number, as in propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol.

items.prompt: A compound has both an OH group and a carboxylic acid group. In its IUPAC name, how is the OH shown?

options.label: As the suffix -ol, since every OH group takes that ending
As the prefix methyl-, since the OH attaches to the chain
As the prefix hydroxy-, since the acid group takes priority
As the suffix -ol, with the acid shown as a prefix

items.explain: When a higher priority group such as a carboxylic acid is present, the prefix hydroxy- is used for the OH.

items.prompt: A label names a substance ending in -ol, such as cholesterol. What does that ending typically suggest about it?

options.label: It contains no oxygen at all
It is a metal-based powder
It is a fatty acid
It is an alcohol

items.explain: The suffix -ol in non-IUPAC names such as paracetamol or cholesterol also typically indicates that the substance is an alcohol.

items.prompt: Before it named a drinkable liquid, what did the word 'alcohol' originally refer to?

options.label: The flammable vapors that rise from boiling wine
A very fine powder made by heating the mineral stibnite
A cosmetic oil pressed from plants and spices
The salt that is added to wine before it is boiled

items.explain: The term was originally used for the very fine powder from sublimating stibnite, and its meaning was later extended to distilled substances and then narrowed to ethanol.

items.prompt: A chemist attaches an OH group to a hydrocarbon. What does that do to its relationship with water?

options.label: It becomes water-attracted
It becomes water-repelling
It becomes unable to react
It becomes a gas in water

items.explain: The OH group confers hydrophilic, water-attracted properties on hydrocarbons.
